title: Change an Employee's Manager
goal: Move one employee to a new line manager in Oracle with the right effective date, then close the loop with the people affected.
context: Screen steps are taken from the HCM job aid 'Change Employee Manager in Oracle Cloud' (last updated 3/2/26, Alex Enferadi). DRAFT FOR SME REVIEW: the pay type check, the 'tell the new manager' step and the call with the outgoing manager describe sensible practice but are not from a published SOP. Confirm them and the contacts with the HCM Academy team.

steps.title: Find the employee
steps.instruction: From the Oracle Home page, search for the employee.
steps.where: The search box on the Home page.
steps.expect: The employee appears in the results with a drop-down arrow next to their name.
steps.why: Starting from the person record makes sure you are changing the right employee.
steps.note: Another way in: Home, Our Workforce tab, Show More under Quick Actions, Employment section, Change Manager. Then search for the employee there. If you use that route, skip the next step.
hints: Check the name against the person number before you go on. Similar names are the most common way this goes wrong.

steps.title: Choose Change Manager
steps.instruction: Select the drop-down arrow next to the employee's name and choose Change Manager.
steps.where: The small arrow to the right of the employee's name in the search results.
steps.expect: The Change Manager page opens on Info to Include.

commonMistakes.say: Change Location moves where someone works. A new supervisor with no other change is Change Manager.
Change Assignment is for job, grade or department changes. Use it only if more than the manager is changing.

steps.title: Info to Include
steps.instruction: Do not change anything on the Info to Include page. Select Continue.
steps.where: Continue is at the bottom of the Info to Include section.
steps.expect: The next section opens with the question: When does the manager change start?

steps.title: Check the pay type
steps.instruction: Before you pick a date, check whether the employee is exempt or non-exempt.
steps.why: The pay type decides which effective dates are allowed.

steps.title: Set the effective date
steps.instruction: Enter the date for "When does the manager change start?"
steps.where: The first field in the section.
steps.expect: The date shows in the field.
hints: For a non-exempt employee, open a calendar and pick the Sunday that starts the pay period the change should begin in.

steps.title: How the manager is changing
steps.instruction: For "What's the way to change the manager?" choose Manager Change.

steps.title: Why the manager is changing
steps.instruction: For "Why are you changing the manager?" choose Change Line Manager.
steps.where: The next drop-down in the same section.
steps.expect: The field shows Change Line Manager.
steps.why: Action reasons drive reporting. The wrong reason makes this look like a different kind of change in the audit trail.

steps.title: Move to Managers
steps.where: At the bottom of the section you just filled in.
steps.expect: The Managers section opens and shows the employee's active manager.

steps.title: Edit the active manager
steps.instruction: Select the pencil icon next to the active manager assigned to the employee.
steps.where: At the right end of the manager's row.
steps.expect: The row opens for editing, with the current manager's name in the Managers field.

steps.title: Assign the new manager
steps.instruction: Delete the active manager's name, search for the new manager in the Managers field, and select the correct manager from the list.
steps.where: The Managers field in the row you are editing.
steps.expect: The new manager's name shows in the Managers field.
steps.why: Picking from the list ties the change to the right person record.
hints: If two managers have similar names, check the title or department shown in the list before you choose.

steps.title: Save
steps.where: On the manager row you are editing.
steps.expect: The row closes and shows the new manager.

steps.title: Submit
steps.where: At the top right of the page.
steps.expect: Oracle confirms the change was submitted.
steps.why: Save only stores your edit on this page. Nothing changes for the employee until you submit.

steps.title: Tell the new manager
steps.instruction: Let the new manager know the change is in and the date it starts.
steps.why: From the effective date, timecards and absence requests route to the new manager. They should hear it from you, not from a surprise approval.
steps.confirm: I let the new manager know

steps.title: Hand off with the outgoing manager
steps.instruction: Call the outgoing manager to hand off anything still waiting on them.

prep.goal: Agree who handles open approvals for this employee up to the effective date.
prep.opener: Hi, quick one. The manager change is submitted and I want to make sure nothing open gets stranded before it takes effect.

pushbacks.if: I was not told about this change
pushbacks.try: Stay factual: say who requested it and the date, and offer to connect them with the requester today.

pushbacks.if: I still have timecards to approve
pushbacks.try: Agree a cut-off: they approve everything dated before the effective date, the new manager takes it from there.

doThis: Say the effective date in your first two sentences.
Ask what is still open for this employee.
End with who does what by when.

callouts.say: For non-exempt employees, the effective date must be the first day of the pay period, which is a Sunday.
callouts.source: Change Employee Manager in Oracle Cloud, job aid updated 3/2/26

callouts.say: Manager changes are approved automatically in Oracle. A confirmation notification is sent shortly after you submit.
callouts.source: Change Employee Manager in Oracle Cloud, job aid updated 3/2/26

reminders.say: Check that the confirmation notification arrived and the new manager shows on the employee's record.

recap.summary: You changed an employee's line manager with a pay-period-safe effective date, told the new manager, and handed off open items with the outgoing manager.
